name: Generation four - the machine-written workshop
hypothesis: A loop with no tools can write, measure and rewrite a strategy until one attempt beats the best sealed result on record.
mechanism: strategy.py is GENERATED by a seat that cannot write files; it returns Python as a string and the sandbox parses it before anything imports it.
data: 5m candles, five USDT majors, via the shared catalogue
the intraday harness's cached indicator panels

helped.what: Volatility-scaled entry bar (asset's own measured daily volatility instead of a fixed 3% opening range)
helped.effect: the sealed-window collapse is gone: 65 trades in 2026 against the incumbent's 24, and 27/68/74/96/103/96/116/111/91 per year - stable through bull AND bear, which is what a regime-neutral bar should do

helped.what: The forensic refusal count that produced the diagnosis
helped.effect: the fixed 3% bar was refused 319,662 times in 2026 and the trend filter only ten - which is how a fixed percentage was identified as a different rule in every volatility regime

helped.what: A sandbox that PARSES generated code before anything imports it
helped.effect: the only reason an unattended seat is allowed to author strategy.py at all; code that could reach the filesystem or the network is refused rather than sandboxed

hurt.effect: +495.35% training at 20.91% drawdown - the best this laboratory has ever measured - produced -5.81% sealed 2026. Gross was -0.87%; the toll on 65 round trips was 4.9%
correct and useless. The bar WAS regime-dependent, fixing it restored the trade count, and firing twenty times more often paid the toll twenty times more often rather than manufacturing an edge

hurt.what: An overnight loop nobody was measuring
hurt.effect: 173 attempts across nine hours produced exactly one training result and never opened 2026, while the watchdog reported 'ok' every thirty minutes throughout
116 of those 173 attempts were spent asking a subscription that had already refused, once a minute, against two reset windows

hurt.what: A gate keyed on FunctionDef and ClassDef only
hurt.effect: 17 attempts refused for CORRECT code - ast.Lambda is neither, so every `key=lambda item: ...` reported that `item` was not available

open.what: Whether a machine-written strategy can beat a hand-written one at all
open.why: the generation-four loop never produced a candidate that reached a sealed reading, so the question was abandoned rather than answered

rules: Making a configuration trade MORE often pays the toll more often; it does not manufacture an edge. Anyone proposing to rescue a configuration by raising its frequency owes an answer to generation four.
+495% training producing a forward loss is the strongest anti-prediction datum on record here: training return does not rank forward return.
A gate that refuses CORRECT code fails silently and is as bad as one that permits bad code - the author is told a rule it is breaking, the rule does not exist, and it cannot comply.
A watchdog that reports 'ok' while nothing is achieved is not a watchdog. Liveness is not progress, and only progress is worth alerting on.

results.verdict: Not promoted. The diagnosis was confirmed and the fix did not pay.
